thread.title: What Analysts are hoping about Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s WWDC event?

author: Grant Pasek
title: What Analysts are hoping about Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s WWDC event?
text:
June 4, 2018 What Analysts are hoping about Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s WWDC event?
The expectations towards the Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) aren’t particularly high time as today is the day, Apple Inc.’s annual WWDC (Worldwide Developers Conference) to be held. WWDC is one of company’s biggest events of the year, along with Apple’s September iPhone release event. But the recent conferences of the company haven’t brought forth much, and put ice on the fire, as not showing off in the way of groundbreaking technology.
The fans of Apple Inc. (AAPL) were pretty much aware, ahead of WWDC that it was going to announce a voice-controlled speaker, in last year WWDC, and also some of its computers upgrade, along with the same kind of software improvements.
If we look at rumors, at this time, no noteworthy hardware rumors in the air about it, although the analysts have been actively speculating over time on time about what could be announced by the tech company during a keynote address, that will takes place on June 4 at 1 p.m. Eastern Time.
There are chances that new surprises will come out this year that will chill the investors with a big hardware or software announcement, but according to experts are mainly expecting incremental enhancements, on both sides, the software and hardware.
Gene Munster, a former Apple analyst at Piper Jaffray, also speaks about the hardware upgrade that most probably Apple could introduce a cheaper Siri-integrated speaker.
“We believe Apple can advance its digital assistant ambitions with a $250 Beats-branded option that does not compromise HomePod’s $349 price point,” Munster wrote.
KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst Andy Hargreaves told that “They’ve missed the mark in recent years,”.
Apple has made augmented reality a major focus, but that “hasn’t caught on yet,” according to Hargreaves. And he said that while the company hasn’t released its own data on Apple Pay Cash, a peer-to-peer money-transfer offering announced last year, the service “doesn’t seem to have impacted Venmo in any way.” About Grant Pasek
